we have developed and characterized a new MR-guidable FUS array for transcranial neuromodulation of non-human primates, with a focus size of 2.3 mm, grating lobing less than 1.5 dB at 3.2 mm, and a peak directivity of 7.2.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the randomization of the transducer elements can reduce the number of elements and thus the cost of the transducer while maintaining a high level of directivity.

a randomized transducer can be designed for MR-guided neuromodulation, and that the focus can be accurately modelled and measured using a combination of optical tracking, acoustic measurements and simulations.

a random phased array can be designed to provide a high degree of directivity while still maintaining a large aperture and a small number of elements, thus reducing the cost and complexity of a transducer.
